data.question: Can employees sign in with SAML 2.0?
Can our HTTPS webhook receive account events from the platform?

candidates.content:
# Employee provisioning

SCIM 2.0 creates, updates, and deactivates employee accounts.
Employees still use the configured sign-in method to authenticate.

# Authentication

Employees can sign in with SAML 2.0.
An admin configures it in Settings > SSO.

# Session policies

Admins set an idle timeout for employee sessions after sign-in.
This policy applies regardless of the sign-in protocol.

# API credentials

Integrations use OAuth 2.0 client credentials to obtain API tokens.
API tokens identify integrations, not employees.

# Webhook signing

Each webhook POST includes an HMAC-SHA256 signature header.
An integration verifies the signature against its endpoint secret.

# Account event webhooks

An admin registers an HTTPS endpoint in Settings > Webhooks.
The platform sends account events to that endpoint.
Failed attempts are retried for up to 24 hours.

# Account event catalog

The platform records account.created, account.updated, and account.deactivated.
Each record includes an event ID and occurrence timestamp.

# Event history API

Clients fetch recorded account events with GET /v1/events.
The endpoint returns pages ordered by occurrence timestamp.

# Webhook signing

Each webhook POST includes an HMAC-SHA256 signature header.
An integration verifies the signature against its endpoint secret.

# Employee provisioning

SCIM 2.0 creates, updates, and deactivates employee accounts.
Employees still use the configured sign-in method to authenticate.
